summary: Established a coding-agent utility gate and a dated append-only audit trail for canonical knowledge changes.
rationale: Paper-level ingestion can add redundant or weakly actionable material that reduces retrieval precision and raises maintenance cost.
practical_impact: Future promotions must be novel, decision-relevant, actionable or testable, evidence-bounded, and accompanied by a dated change record.

summary: Added a narrow navigable-source tool and regression-test contract to the existing iterative retrieval pattern.
rationale: Stable source-local positions, explicit seen-result handling and separated mutation authority close an operational gap without duplicating established agentic RAG patterns or promoting vendor benchmarks.
practical_impact: Document-research and coding agents can now be tested for anchor-preserving navigation, repeat-result termination, tenant isolation and read-only retrieval authority.

summary: Improved coding-agent discoverability with a dedicated knowledge lane, technique-card cross-links, AGENTS.md consumption contract, retrieval eval cases, and a compile-generated technique index.
rationale: Coding-agent content was searchable but weakly connected through lanes, pattern-to-card links, and retrieval regression coverage compared with RAG and security topics.
practical_impact: Coding agents can now enter through a curated lane, resolve technique_id paths deterministically, and be regression-tested for harness, instruction, skill, and replay queries.

summary: Restricted the relaxed search fallback to selective terms and added a calibrated match confidence signal plus a read-first navigation and scope contract for agents.
rationale: The previous OR fallback matched filler tokens, so out-of-scope questions returned confident-looking noise with no signal that the topic is uncovered.
practical_impact: Out-of-scope queries now report low or none confidence with an advisory, the coverage floor is calibrated against the labelled retrieval pack, and agents are directed to navigate and load canonical sections before searching.

summary: Separated the human entry point in README.md from toolchain and governance internals, moving the latter into a new docs/contributing.md, and corrected a stale description of the search fallback in docs/architecture.md.
rationale: README.md had grown to duplicate setup and search instructions and led with internal governance rules instead of what the knowledge base covers, while its search description no longer matched the selective-term fallback and confidence signal already shipped.
practical_impact: README.md is now a short human-first overview that still preserves the setup, quality-check, and public-API pointers relied on by AGENTS.md and the generated index.md; repository layout, the promotion gate, and the full command reference now live in docs/contributing.md; and docs/architecture.md documents the actual retrieval fallback and confidence behavior.

summary: Added a required technique-card lifecycle with an audited retirement gate, and defaulted search to reviewed and contested pages so immature or retired material no longer answers questions.
rationale: The retirement machinery existed for pages and claims but had never been used, and did not exist at all for technique cards, so all 132 cards presented as equally current and the catalogue could only grow. Search additionally applied no status filter by default, admitting inbox and draft sections into results.
practical_impact: Every card now declares recommended, situational, legacy or deprecated. Legacy and deprecated cards require a retirement reason and an applied supersession record in the change ledger, which an ordinary technique record does not satisfy, and lint rejects successors that are unknown, self-referential, retired or cyclic, plus live cards that carry retirement metadata. technique-index.json publishes lifecycle and successors on the exact-lookup path. Search omits inbox, draft, superseded and archived unless --any-status is passed and reports status_filter_source. All existing cards were seeded as situational, so recommended is scarce and must be granted alongside the routing page that names the family default.

summary: Promoted nine routing-default technique cards to recommended and updated the parser, chunking, retrieval and coding-agent catalog pages to name them explicitly.
rationale: Every card had been seeded situational, so agents had no deterministic default despite routing pages already naming PyMuPDF, Docling, recursive splitting, BM25, dense retrieval and the three coding-agent harness cards as first choices.
practical_impact: technique-index.json now exposes nine recommended defaults; agents should propose these first and escalate only when use_when or routing conditions say otherwise. Retrieval eval cases for parser and chunking defaults were added and verified.

summary: Retired fixed token windows to legacy as an ablation-only control and named recursive boundary-aware splitting as the production baseline.
rationale: The chunking routing defaults already treat recursive splitting as the cheap production baseline and fixed windows as a reproducible control; leaving both situational let agents treat them as equally recommendable.
practical_impact: chunking.fixed.token-window is legacy with superseded_by chunking.fixed.recursive-split; the chunking catalog now states fixed windows are ablation-only. Retrieval eval cases for the chunking default were checked and still pass.

summary: Added optional online, offline-snapshot, and MCP retrieval clients with a trust contract for a separately indexed external discovery corpus.
rationale: Useful secondary guides should remain retrievable for alternatives and research hypotheses without entering canonical search results or weakening the knowledge-admission gate.
practical_impact: Coding agents can request separately labelled KB and EXT candidates through a deterministic public endpoint, a digest-checked offline snapshot, or a read-only stdio MCP tool; external material remains non-canonical, untrusted, date- and source-pinned, and incapable of automatic promotion.

summary: Added JIT-Agent as a reviewed source and a narrow experimental contract for instance-conditioned harness synthesis.
rationale: The paper and public artifacts add a novel per-task harness-generation mechanism, while missing replication, incomplete streaming-evolution artifacts and unsafe generated-code execution prevent promotion to a production default or RSI evidence.
practical_impact: Coding-agent architects may evaluate generated per-task harnesses only as sandboxed challengers against fixed harnesses and cheaper routers, with complete-cost accounting, protected paired replay, external promotion authority and rollback.

summary: Added a primary-source audit that separates complexity routing, sufficiency-and-gap judging, corpus adaptation, reasoning-time retrieval and trained search policies.
rationale: Recent retrieval-loop names overlap in purpose but differ materially in controller location, training requirements, latency risk and evaluation scope, so a mechanism-level audit is more useful than separate uncontextualized technique cards.
practical_impact: Architects can route modern retrieval-control approaches by mechanism and maturity while retaining explicit local replay requirements and avoiding unsupported universal latency claims.

summary: Added an owner-reported latency case candidate and a draft composition for selective parallel domain fan-out, bounded branch retrieval, typed fan-in and one final synthesis.
rationale: Existing material covers routers, gap-guided retrieval, typed delegation and budgets separately but does not make their multi-domain composition, straggler boundary and evidence-preserving fan-in explicit.
practical_impact: The reported architecture now has a testable vendor-neutral candidate with explicit failure modes, paired baselines, shadow rollout, independent kill switches and a clear evidence gate before promotion.

summary: Added a revision-pinned official source for Qwen3-32B and bounded its use to a case-specific retrieval-controller challenger.
rationale: The owner selected Qwen3-32B as a possible controller, but interface support for thinking control and tools must remain separate from unmeasured claims about sufficiency accuracy, latency and superiority over smaller models.
practical_impact: The draft pattern can now cite verified model properties while requiring pinned serving conditions and paired controller replays before Qwen3-32B becomes an architecture choice.

summary: Added HarnessDev evidence and a provisional fixed-executor, protected-holdout gate for persistent agent-harness evolution.
rationale: The reported mismatch between visible feedback, held-out outcomes and executor transfer shows that a runnable or feedback-improved harness cannot safely be treated as retained capability without separating creator, harness, executor and evaluator variables.
practical_impact: Harness candidates must now be frozen, replayed on protected tasks with a fixed executor, checked across supported executors, costed across creation and execution, and retained only behind canary and rollback controls.

summary: Closed architecture-relevant evaluation gaps with one cross-cutting operations pattern and narrow updates for stochastic model identity, RAG metric semantics, CI gates, tracing, resilience, FinOps and incident response.
rationale: The evaluation lane covered metric and rollout design but lacked a compact production contract; consolidating the gaps avoids vendor pages, course material and duplicate technique cards.
practical_impact: Architects can now connect eval evidence to trace sampling, fault injection, cost attribution, SLO alerts, runbooks and postmortem-derived regression while keeping Python/Git/pandas education and generic portfolio advice out of scope.

summary: Added a bounded reward-integrity synthesis backed by BenchShield v1.
rationale: Existing evaluation, runtime and RSI pages did not explicitly separate vulnerability exposure, observed exploitation, sealed reward-chain evidence and semantic adequacy.
practical_impact: Promotion decisions now have a concise contract for authority separation, sealed reward provenance, explicit integrity verdicts, structural replay and fail-closed reward admission without treating a fresh preprint as universal proof.

summary: Filed Wiki Foundation Model (WFM) evidence as a bounded source record plus two small pattern additions.
rationale: The adoptable lesson is representation choice and grounded-versus-permissive grading, not the pretrained graph foundation model; recording it prevents a training-scale artifact from becoming a default.
practical_impact: Architects get a hybrid wiki representation option and a grading-separation rule, with training-scale and context-cost limits stated explicitly.

summary: Added an agent-first debug-loop pattern with phase gates, prompt blocks and anti-pattern detectors.
rationale: Repair-agent evidence shows fixed localize-repair-validate structure can beat more autonomous loops, and that verification must bind to the claimed property rather than to green counts.
practical_impact: Coding-agent fixes now have an observable phase contract: failing reproduction first, disconfirmation before patching, regression gate, fresh-context verification and evidence-bound handoff.

summary: Filed STAIR structure-aware retrieval evidence as a bounded source record with one pattern addition on structure-aware retrieval units.
rationale: The transferable result is that supplying document structure at query time beat memorising hierarchy in a controlled ablation; the headline scores rest on synthetic queries and constrained decoding and are not portable.
practical_impact: Retrieval design now has an explicit option to route by document structure before passage selection, with the parametric-index and update/deletion limits recorded.

summary: Filed SoL-Pi harness auto-research evidence with gate-isolation guidance in the harness pattern and an operating-point clarification in the RSI boundary.
rationale: The transferable contribution is the selection machinery and harness-level token efficiency, while the reported capability cost and the smaller solved-task count on a second benchmark contradict a free-improvement reading.
practical_impact: Harness improvement work now has a concrete gate-isolation design plus an explicit requirement to report efficiency gains together with measured capability cost and per-mechanism activation.

summary: Filed coding-agent skill distillation evidence as a bounded source record plus conditions for replacing a held-out gate with a single offline pass.
rationale: The paper's single-pass offline distillation beats gated search under matched data access but drops to two of four benchmarks once baselines receive more data and environment access, and it omits corpus construction cost and outcome variance.
practical_impact: Offline prompt distillation is now recorded as a bounded cheaper operating point that requires verified corpus representativeness, counted corpus cost and reported variance before it may replace the gated loop.
